Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for up to 85% of lung cancer cases, with activating EGFR mutations present in 10–15% of Western and up to 35% of Asian patients. EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have transformed management, with first-line osimertinib demonstrating a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 18.9 months and overall survival (OS) of 38.6 months in the FLAURA trial. However, resistance inevitably develops, most commonly via T790M mutations (~50% of cases after first- and second-generation TKIs), and after osimertinib, through diverse mechanisms including C797S mutations, MET/HER2 amplification, and histologic transformation.
